subject: ss-general-medicine
title: Endocrinology in pregnancy and special situations

steps.tx: Screening for **gestational diabetes** is a key antenatal task. A **75-gram oral glucose tolerance test** is usually done at 24 to 28 weeks in women without high risk features. Women with obesity or polycystic ovary syndrome should be screened at the first visit. A fasting glucose above 100 mg/dL in a thin patient raises the possibility of MODY rather than GDM, so genetic or family history clues matter.
steps.say: Screening for gestational diabetes is a key task in antenatal care. A 75-gram oral glucose tolerance test is usually done between 24 and 28 weeks in women without high risk features. Women with obesity or polycystic ovary syndrome should be screened at the first visit. A fasting glucose above 100 milligrams per decilitre in a thin patient raises the possibility of MODY rather than gestational diabetes, so family history and genetic clues matter.

steps.tx: The **IADPSG** consensus defines **gestational diabetes** when any single value on a 75-gram oral glucose tolerance test reaches its threshold. Three timepoints are checked: fasting, one hour and two hours after the glucose load. Only one abnormal value is needed for diagnosis, so a single result is enough to make the label. Check current ICMR and NMC guidance, as local protocols may differ from these international thresholds.
steps.say: The IADPSG consensus defines gestational diabetes when any single value on a 75 gram glucose tolerance test reaches its threshold. Three timepoints are checked: fasting, one hour and two hours after the glucose load. One abnormal value is enough for diagnosis. Check current ICMR and NMC guidance, because local protocols may differ from these international thresholds.

steps.tx: After **gestational diabetes**, a repeat **75-gram OGTT** is done 4 to 12 weeks after delivery to detect persistent dysglycaemia. Women with prior GDM carry up to a seven-fold higher risk of **type 2 diabetes** than normoglycaemic women. Long-term screening should continue, at least every three years, with lifestyle advice from the outset.
steps.say: After gestational diabetes, a repeat 75-gram glucose tolerance test is done four to twelve weeks after delivery to detect persistent dysglycaemia. Women with prior gestational diabetes carry up to a seven-fold higher risk of type 2 diabetes than women with normal pregnancies. Long-term screening should continue, at least every three years, with lifestyle advice given from the outset.

steps.tx: In normal pregnancy, **human placental lactogen** drives **insulin resistance** and increased lipolysis. This diverts maternal glucose and fats towards the fetus. When maternal beta cells cannot raise insulin output to match this demand, hyperglycaemia develops. Excess fetal glucose stimulates fetal insulin, which promotes fetal growth and macrosomia.

steps.tx: Glucocorticoid potency is compared against a reference agent, so clinicians convert a current dose into an **equivalent dose** of another steroid before changing treatment. Equivalence tables are only a guide, because potency and duration of action differ between agents. For **perioperative steroid cover**, patients taking long term glucocorticoids may need extra doses around surgery to prevent an **adrenal crisis**. Any change should be agreed with an endocrinologist.
